subject: Re: Redwood model fit & benchmark links — follow-up + next steps
messages:
From: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finexa.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model recommendations & benchmarks

Alex — thanks again for the run-through earlier. A couple quick asks so we can evaluate fit on our side:  

- Could you share the Redwood-verified performance profiles for the models you recommended (TPS guidance, p50/p95 latency)? We need to understand tail latency for a chat use case (avg token size ~30, average response length ~60 tokens).  
- We have an initial prompt set (sample production prompts + edge cases) — would you accept that for a quick quality eval? I attached the prompt set to this thread.
- Primary constraints: low latency (p95 < 200ms ideally), and sustained throughput around 80–120 TPS for peak traffic.

Also, security/compliance is a factor — can you point me to SOC2 evidence and the data retention policy for hosted inference?

Thanks,
Sam Keller
Head of Product
Finexa
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finexa.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model recommendations & benchmarks

Sam — great to connect today. Short recap + next steps below. Thanks for sending the prompt set (received).

Recap of call:
- Primary use case: low-latency chat for customer support; avg payloads ~30 tokens, responses ~60 tokens; expected peak 80–120 TPS.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 200ms, predictable cost per 1k tokens, and no quality regressions after model updates.

Initial model recommendations (based on your constraints):
1) redwood-rlhf-7b-quant (recommended) — best latency/cost balance for short responses; we see 80–150 TPS on an n1-dedicated pool with continuous batching and prefix KV caching.
2) redwood-13b-quant (high-quality fallback) — higher quality on longer/edge-case prompts; expect p95 ~220–350ms depending on sequence length, but better semantic accuracy.
3) redwood-8k-llamaX (experimental) — if you prioritize lower tail latency for very short responses.

What we’re sharing:
- Redwood-verified perf profiles: TPS guidance, p50/p95/p99 latency percentiles and token throughput for the above variants. Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/finexa-2026 (attached PDF: redwood_benchmark_finexa_20260518.pdf)
- Prompt set you shared (attached as finexa_prompt_set_v1.json).

Quality/regression controls we recommend:
- Baseline eval: run your prompt set against the recommended model(s) and record top-line metrics (accuracy/intent-match, hallucination rate on a labeled subset).
- Continuous eval: Redwood Optimize can run periodic checks and trigger regression alerts tied to your prompt sets; on regression we can automatically rollback to the last verified model variant.

Next steps / asks:
1) We’ll run a 24–48 hour throughput & quality eval using your prompt set on the redwood-rlhf-7b-quant variant. Please confirm any IP/data handling restrictions for the eval.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Marissa (solutions engineer) and Dylan (SRE) to validate infra sizing and latency SLOs. Marissa — are you available Tue/Wed next week?
3) Share expected concurrency pattern (burst length, steady-state) and sample payload sizes so we can pick the right dedicated pool and batching config.

I’ve attached the benchmark PDF and included a link to the Redwood perf profile page. If perf looks good we can propose a Dedicated capacity plan (FNX-2026-0042) with a canary rollout and SLA.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_finexa_20260518.pdf, finexa_prompt_set_v1.json
From: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finexa.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.ortiz@finexa.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model recommendations & benchmarks

Thanks Alex — that all looks sensible. Quick answers:  

- IP/data handling: you can use the prompt set for benchmarking; do not persist any Finexa PII in logs. We’ll provide an anonymized variant if needed.
- Concurrency: steady-state ~60 TPS, bursts up to ~120 TPS for ~3–5 minutes.
- Availability for deep-dive: Tue May 26 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed May 27 14:00–15:00 PT. Prefer Tue if possible.

Elena and I will review the benchmark PDF and come back with any questions. Please send SOC2 link and any data retention notes.

—Sam
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finexa.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model recommendations & benchmarks — scheduling + next steps

Sam — thanks for the quick responses and for confirming concurrency patterns. Per below I’ve looped in Marissa and Dylan to handle the technical deep-dive and the live eval.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Redwood: start an eval run on redwood-rlhf-7b-quant using finexa_prompt_set_v1.json (24–48h). We’ll run perf and quality checks and share a results dashboard + the benchmark PDF update. (Owner: alex_martinez)
- Finexa: send anonymized prompt set if you prefer PII scrubbed, and confirm whether we can capture aggregated latency metrics for the eval (not raw PII). (Owner: Sam)
- Schedule: Marissa will set up the deep-dive for Tue May 26 10:00 PT and share the calendar invite + a short pre-read. (Owner: marissa_cole)

Docs & links: SOC2 overview — https://docs.redwood.com/soc2-report; Data retention summary — https://docs.redwood.com/data-retention. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

We’ll include a short regression policy in the eval report: if we observe a drop >5% in intent-match or a >10% increase in hallucination rate versus your labeled baseline, we’ll flag and recommend rolling back to the verified variant.

Marissa / Dylan — can you confirm calendar availability and whether we should provision a short-lived dedicated pool for the 24–48h run (cost estimate attached in the benchmark PDF)?

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
